issue.subject: A repair notebook, an open bench, and a useful habit
issue.preheader: Three practical ideas from our fictional makerspace notes.
issue.intro: This is an original fictional newsletter for the workshop. Each quoted passage below is attached to a supplied source note; the surrounding commentary is editable editorial writing.

sections.heading: Start with the repair notebook
sections.quote: Write down the symptom before changing a part.
sections.commentary: A useful notebook captures what you observed, what you tried, and what changed. Use the first page of your next project to make those distinctions explicit.

sections.heading: What to bring to the open bench
sections.quote: Bring one small project and a written description of the next step.
sections.commentary: A small, specific next step gives a helper something concrete to respond to. This is a fictional exercise announcement, not an invitation to a real event.

sections.heading: Leave a map for the next person
sections.quote: Store the editable file beside the exported version.
sections.commentary: Today's workshop applies that idea directly: your ZIP includes the finished issue and the workspace that generated it. Change the workspace, then create a new edition.

sources.title: Fictional Mossworks repair notebook
sources.text: Original fictional workshop source. Write down the symptom before changing a part. Record the change separately from your explanation of why it helped. Keep unsuccessful attempts in the notebook too.

sources.title: Fictional open-bench briefing
sources.text: Original fictional workshop source. Bring one small project and a written description of the next step. The exercise uses no real venue, schedule, or registration page.

sources.title: Fictional project handoff notes
sources.text: Original fictional workshop source. Store the editable file beside the exported version. Include the original inputs so the next person can modify the result instead of starting again.
